**As** an agile user
**I want to** see an easy-to-understand burndown graph
**so that** I can quickly see how the sprint is going

**Acceptance criteria**
*   The y-axis shows the sum of story points.
*   The x-axis shows the days between the sprint start and finish date.
*   The graph shows three data series: Remaining story points, Guideline, Remaining story points (projection).
*   Non-working days show as a gray bar with lower opacity.
*   A blankslate shows instead of a graph if the sprint lacks start and end dates, if the current date is before the sprint start date, or if no work package has a story point set.
*   The graph is visible if the user can see the sprint.

**Technical notes**
*   The y-axis unit needs to be flexible later.
*   The x-axis date format needs to be consistent with the Dashboard charts.
*   Remaining story points is the sum of story points per hour for open work packages.
*   The story point value uses the end of each hour or the current time, whichever is earlier.
*   The series stops at the current date if that is earlier than the sprint finish date.
*   The Guideline starts at the sum of story points at the sprint start and ends at 0 at the planned finish date.
*   The Guideline declines at a constant rate on working days.
*   The Guideline ignores story point changes after the sprint start.
*   The Guideline points to the planned date if the sprint runs longer than planned.
*   The projection starts where Remaining story points ends and decreases to 0 in a straight line.
*   The projection only exists if the sprint is ongoing and the current time is before the planned end.
*   Chart.js shows specific data points on hover.

**Permissions and visibility considerations**
*   The feature is visible to users who can see the sprint.

**Translation considerations**
*   Key terms include Story points, Guideline, and Remaining story points (projection).

metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so, the work package name in the running timer section isn't clickable. Here's what I did and saw. I started a timer in a work package. Then I clicked the user avatar in the top-right corner, the one with a small icon showing a timer is running. A side-sheet opens on the right, and above the usual entries there's a time tracking section. It shows the work package I'm running the timer for. When I click the name of that work package, nothing happens. So the buggy behavior is that the displayed work package name isn't linked to anything and doesn't open the work package. What I'd expect is that clicking the work package with the running timer in the right side-sheet takes me to that work package. Here's the screen capture: Environment info: - Community - OpenProject 17.7 - Zen 1.21.3b (Firefox 152.0.1) - Mac OS X 15.7.4 - Language: EN

What's going wrong: * If the tooltip opens to the bottom, it gets cut off because there isn't enough space. * The direction the tooltip opens in seems to depend on where the cursor came from before hovering the milestone. What I'd expect: tooltips should never be cut off, no matter which direction the cursor approaches from. Screenshot (attached): Environment: OpenProject version is unreleased, dev branch ahead of 17.8. Browser is Firefox (Chrome, Safari, Mobile Safari and Other are not checked). OS is Linux (Ubuntu). Windows, Mac OS X, Mobile iOS, Mobile Android, Chrome OS and Other are not checked.
metadata.reconstructedTicket: ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a project with multiple milestones. 2. Do not add sprints or project phases. 3. Navigate to the project overview page. 4. Locate the project timeline. 5. Hover over a milestone. ### What is the buggy behavior? * The tooltip renders downward and clips at the bottom edge. * Vertical space limitations cause the cutoff. * Tooltip direction changes based on cursor entry angle. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. The application repositions the tooltip to prevent clipping. 2. The tooltip remains fully visible regardless of cursor approach direction. ### Screenshots and other files ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** * [x] Packaged installation **OpenProject version** Unreleased dev branch (ahead of v17.8) **Browser** * [x] Firefox **Operating System** * [x] Linux (Ubuntu)

**Browser**
* Firefox 140.0.4

**Operating System**
* Windows

What goes wrong is one of these: - the image isn't showing at all - the image only shows when the left side menu is collapsed - the text overlaps the image What I'd expect is that Windows users can see the images and text properly. Screenshots: Environment: - OpenProject version: 16.2.1 - Browser: Firefox 140.0.4 (not Chrome, Safari, Mobile Safari or Other) - Operating system: Windows (not Mac OS X, Mobile iOS, Mobile Android, Linux, Chrome OS or Other)
metadata.reconstructedTicket: ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use a Windows laptop with 150% display scaling. 2. metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so here's the bug. Changing a project's identifier fails if there's a required project attribute that the existing project doesn't have a value for. To reproduce: log in as a user who can create projects and project attributes. There needs to be at least one existing project. If there isn't one, click the green + in the top-left corner, then **+ Project**. Fill in **Name** (e.g. Example Project) plus any other required fields, then click "Save". The project should save and redirect to the Project Overview page of the new project. Next, create a **new project attribute that is required for all projects**: - Click the avatar in the right-hand corner, then **Administration**. - On the administration page, click **Projects**, then **Project attributes**. - Click the green **+ Project attribute**. - Fill in **Name** (e.g. New Project Attribute). - Select a default Section. - Check **Required for all Projects**. - Click **Save**. Then select the project I created earlier in the project selector at the top of the page and click **Project settings**. Click **Change Identifier**, type in a new identifier and click **Update**. What goes wrong is that an error message appears saying "New project attribute can't be blank". The project is now in an inconsistent state too. There's a screenshot of the error: Expected behavior: the identifier should just be updated. Environment: - OpenProject installation type: community.openproject.org - Browser: Chrome (checked), Firefox (not checked), Safari (checked), Mobile Safari (not checked), Other (not checked) - Operating System: Mac OS X (checked). Windows, Mobile iOS, Mobile Android, Linux, Chrome OS and Other are not checked. - Language: en_GB

metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so here's the bug. Changing a project's identifier fails if there's a required project attribute that the existing project doesn't have a value for. The project should save and redirect to the Project Overview page of the new project. Next, create a **new project attribute that is required for all projects**: - Click the avatar in the right-hand corner, then **Administration**. - On the administration page, click **Projects**, then **Project attributes**. - Click the green **+ Project attribute**. - Fill in **Name** (e.g. New Project Attribute). - Select a default Section. - Check **Required for all Projects**. - Click **Save**. Then select the project I created earlier in the project selector at the top of the page and click **Project settings**. Click **Change Identifier**, type in a new identifier and click **Update**. What goes wrong is that an error message appears saying "New project attribute can't be blank". The project is now in an inconsistent state too. There's a screenshot of the error: Expected behavior: the identifier should just be updated. Windows, Mobile iOS, Mobile Android, Linux, Chrome OS and Other are not checked. - Language: en_GB

### Steps to reproduce
1. Log in as a user who can create projects and project attributes.
2. Ensure at least one existing project exists.
3. If no project exists, click the green + in the top-left corner, then + Project.
4. Fill in Name e.g. Example Project plus any other required fields, then click "Save".
5. The project saves and redirects to the Project Overview page of the new project.
6. Create a new project attribute that is required for all projects.
7. Click the avatar in the right-hand corner, then Administration.
8. On the administration page, click Projects, then Project attributes.
9. Click the green + Project attribute.
10. Fill in Name e.g. New Project Attribute.
11. Select a default Section.
12. Check Required for all Projects.
13. Click Save.
14. Select the project created earlier in the project selector at the top of the page and click Project settings.
15. Click Change Identifier, type in a new identifier and click Update.

### What is the buggy behavior?
* An error message appears saying "New project attribute can't be blank".
* The project is now in an inconsistent state.

### What is the expected behavior?
* The identifier should just be updated.

### Screenshots and other files
* A screenshot of the error is provided.

### Environment information
**OpenProject installation type**
* community.openproject.org

**Browser**
* Chrome checked
* Firefox not checked
* Safari checked
* Mobile Safari not checked
* Other not checked

**Operating System**
* Mac OS X checked
* Windows not checked
* Mobile iOS not checked
* Mobile Android not checked
* Linux not checked
* Chrome OS not checked
* Other not checked

**Language**
* en_GB

metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so here's the bug. Changing a project's identifier fails if there's a required project attribute that the existing project doesn't have a value for. To reproduce: log in as a user who can create projects and project attributes. There needs to be at least one existing project. If there isn't one, click the green + in the top-left corner, then **+ Project**. Fill in **Name** (e.g. Example Project) plus any other required fields, then click "Save". The project should save and redirect to the Project Overview page of the new project. Next, create a **new project attribute that is required for all projects**: - Click the avatar in the right-hand corner, then **Administration**. - On the administration page, click **Projects**, then **Project attributes**. - Click the green **+ Project attribute**. - Fill in **Name** (e.g. New Project Attribute). - Select a default Section. - Check **Required for all Projects**. - Click **Save**. Then select the project I created earlier in the project selector at the top of the page and click **Project settings**. Click **Change Identifier**, type in a new identifier and click **Update**. What goes wrong is that an error message appears saying "New project attribute can't be blank". The project is now in an inconsistent state too. There's a screenshot of the error: Expected behavior: the identifier should just be updated. Environment: - OpenProject installation type: community.openproject.org - Browser: Chrome (checked), Firefox (not checked), Safari (checked), Mobile Safari (not checked), Other (not checked) - Operating System: Mac OS X (checked). Windows, Mobile iOS, Mobile Android, Linux, Chrome OS and Other are not checked. - Language: en_GB

### Steps to reproduce

* Log in as a user who can create projects and project attributes.
* Ensure at least one existing project exists. If not:
  * Click the green + in the top-left corner, then **+ Project**.
  * Fill in **Name** (e.g. Example Project) plus any other required fields.
  * Click "Save". The project should save and redirect to the Project Overview page.
* Create a new project attribute that is required for all projects:
  * Click the avatar in the right-hand corner, then **Administration**.
  * On the administration page, click **Projects**, then **Project attributes**.
  * Click the green **+ Project attribute**.
  * Fill in **Name** (e.g. New Project Attribute).
  * Select a default Section.
  * Check **Required for all Projects**.
  * Click **Save**.
* Select the project created earlier in the project selector at the top of the page.
* Click **Project settings**.
* Click **Change Identifier**.
* Type in a new identifier and click **Update**.

### What is the buggy behavior?

* Changing a project's identifier fails if a required project attribute has no value.
* An error message appears: "New project attribute can't be blank".
* The project is in an inconsistent state.

### What is the expected behavior?

* The identifier should be updated.

### Screenshots and other files

* Screenshot of the error

### Environment information

**OpenProject installation type**
* Hosted cloud edition

**Browser**
* Chrome
* Firefox
* Safari
* Mobile Safari

**Operating System**
* Mac OS X

**Language**
* en_GB

* The field width matches the other fields in the dialog.

### Environment information

* OpenProject installation type: Hosted cloud edition (community.openproject.org)
* Browser: Safari
* Operating System: Mac OS X
* Language: en_GB
* Other browsers and operating systems are not applicable.

* Mac OS X

* en_GB

### Steps to reproduce

1. Login as a user with permission to add relations to existing work packages.
2. Go to an existing work package.
3. Click the "Relations" tab.
4. Click the "+ Relation" button.
5. Select any type of relationship.
6. Enter the ID or search criteria of a work package with a long subject in the autocomplete field.

2. The field width matches the other fields in the dialog.

* Log in with an SSO provider
* Go to My account

### What is the buggy behavior?

* The email attribute shows a warning “cannot be changed”
* The warning is incorrect because the email can be changed

### What is the expected behavior?

* The warning is not shown for SSO users
* The warning is only shown for LDAP users

### Screenshots and other files

* Screenshot shows the warning on the email attribute

metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so, bug with exporting Gantt charts in OpenProject. The export files get created but can't be downloaded. To reproduce, I cloned the OP deploy repo from https://github.com/opf/openproject-deploy and started OP with `docker compose up -d`. Then I created a new project with at least 1 task and went to the `Gantt Charts` view. In the upper right corner I clicked the three dots and selected `Export`. 2. Start OpenProject using `docker compose up -d`
3. Create a new project with at least one task

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the OP deploy repository from https://github.com/opf/openproject-deploy
2. Start OpenProject using `docker compose up -d`
3. Create a new project with at least one task
4. Navigate to the Gantt Charts view
5. In the upper right corner, click the three dots and select Export
6. Attempt to download the file in any format

### What is the buggy behavior?

* Export files are created in `files/attachment/file` but cannot be downloaded
* Browser displays "Site wasn't available" error when attempting download
* Server returns 500 status code for the download request
* Error in logs: `undefined method 'path' for nil:NilClass`

### What is the expected behavior?

* Export files should download successfully when requested
* No errors should occur during the download process

### Steps to reproduce
*   Clone the OP deploy repo from https://github.com/opf/openproject-deploy.

*   Select `Export`.

metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so, braindump time. I found a bug in custom fields for spent time. To reproduce: I open Settings, go to custom fields, and choose spent time. The OpenProject version is 12.5.8. I saw it in both Chrome and Firefox (not Safari, Mobile Safari or other). The language was English and German.

metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so, braindump time. I found a bug in custom fields for spent time. To reproduce: I open Settings, go to custom fields, and choose spent time. Then I create a new custom field and pick type float. I set a max or a min value that's a fraction, like 5.5, and when I try to save it doesn't work. What's going wrong is that within custom fields for time spent you can set a max and a min value, but those can't be fractions, even though the field itself is of type float. That doesn't make sense. What I'd expect is that a fraction should be allowed in a float field as a min and max limit. There are two screenshots that go with this: Environment: I saw this on the Docker All-in-one container (not hosted cloud, packaged installation, docker-compose or other). metadata.transformedTicket: Ok so, braindump time. I found a bug in custom fields for spent time. To reproduce: I open Settings, go to custom fields, and choose spent time. Then I create a new custom field and pick type float. I set a max or a min value that's a fraction, like 5.5, and when I try to save it doesn't work. What's going wrong is that within custom fields for time spent you can set a max and a min value, but those can't be fractions, even though the field itself is of type float. That doesn't make sense. What I'd expect is that a fraction should be allowed in a float field as a min and max limit. There are two screenshots that go with this: Environment: I saw this on the Docker All-in-one container (not hosted cloud, packaged installation, docker-compose or other). The OpenProject version is 12.5.8. I saw it in both Chrome and Firefox (not Safari, Mobile Safari or other). The language was English and German.

View the meeting list. ### What is the buggy behavior? * The Duration column always shows hours, e.g. "0.5 h" or "1 h". ### What is the expected behavior? 1. metadata.originalTicket: ### Steps to reproduce * In the Meetings module, go to 'My meetings', 'Recurring meetings' or 'All meetings' * Make sure the list has at least a few upcoming meetings ### What is the buggy behavior? * The Duration column is always expressed in hours * eg. "0.5 h", "1 h" ### What is the expected behavior? * The Duration column should show this information in a more human-friendly format, * eg. "30 minutes", "2 hours" ### Screenshots and other files **Current:** **Mockups:** ### Environment information **Community** **OpenProject 15.1** **Browser:** Firefox, Mac (desktop) **Language** EN

Screenshots: **Current:** **Mockups:** Environment: Community edition, OpenProject 15.1. Browser is Firefox on Mac (desktop). Language is EN.

Select the "Change size" option. ### What is the buggy behavior? * The context menu appears after clicking the link. * The "Change size" dropdown renders partially outside the viewport. * The full menu remains hidden from view. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. The application displays the complete dropdown menu. 2. The menu stays entirely visible within the viewport. ### Screenshots and other files ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** * Hosted cloud edition (QA stage environment) **OpenProject version** * OpenProject 17.5.0 * Core build: 91e885845d84cd0d88a2a6bd485a79c3c9951e8d * Product version: 162437036e3417a33fe5bd3fd4771c1a0019966a **Browser** * [x] Chrome

metadata.originalTicket: ### Description: Several employees reported an issue when using checkbox (task) lists inside a table in a work package description. If a checkbox list item has nested sub-items, the parent (top-level) items become invisible after saving the work package. This happens both when: * the sub-items are **checkboxes**, or * the sub-items are **bulleted list items** under a parent checkbox item. * (I haven't tested the issue on numbered list items) In edit mode, the parent items briefly appear when clicking into the description field, but after saving again, the parent checkbox remains without any visible text/description. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any work package and edit the description. 2. Insert/create a table in the description. 3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list (task list). 4. Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (i.e., a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. ### What is the buggy behavior? * After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible (their text/description disappears). * The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. * When switching back into edit mode (click into the description), the parent items appear briefly. * After saving again, the parent items disappear again. * In the “code view” of the description, the list elements inside the table appear to be output/rendered incorrectly by OpenProject. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should remain visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables should render consistently in both view mode and edit mode. **Additional notes:** * This seems specifically related to checkbox/task lists **inside tables** combined with **nested** checkbox items. ### Screenshots and other files and ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** * Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** * [ ] Chrome * [x] Firefox * [ ] Safari * [ ] Mobile Safari * [x] Edge **Operating System** * [x] Windows * [ ] Mac OS X * [ ] Mobile iOS * [ ] Mobile Android * [ ] Linux (please specify distro) * [ ] Chrome OS * [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

metadata.originalTicket: ### Description: Several employees reported an issue when using checkbox (task) lists inside a table in a work package description. If a checkbox list item has nested sub-items, the parent (top-level) items become invisible after saving the work package. This happens both when: * the sub-items are **checkboxes**, or * the sub-items are **bulleted list items** under a parent checkbox item. * (I haven't tested the issue on numbered list items) In edit mode, the parent items briefly appear when clicking into the description field, but after saving again, the parent checkbox remains without any visible text/description. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any work package and edit the description. 2. Insert/create a table in the description. 3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list (task list). 4. Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (i.e., a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. ### What is the buggy behavior? * After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible (their text/description disappears). * The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. * When switching back into edit mode (click into the description), the parent items appear briefly. * After saving again, the parent items disappear again. * In the “code view” of the description, the list elements inside the table appear to be output/rendered incorrectly by OpenProject. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should remain visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables should render consistently in both view mode and edit mode. **Additional notes:** * This seems specifically related to checkbox/task lists **inside tables** combined with **nested** checkbox items. ### Screenshots and other files and ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** * Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** * [ ] Chrome * [x] Firefox * [ ] Safari * [ ] Mobile Safari * [x] Edge **Operating System** * [x] Windows * [ ] Mac OS X * [ ] Mobile iOS * [ ] Mobile Android * [ ] Linux (please specify distro) * [ ] Chrome OS * [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

metadata.originalTicket: ### Description: Several employees reported an issue when using checkbox (task) lists inside a table in a work package description. If a checkbox list item has nested sub-items, the parent (top-level) items become invisible after saving the work package. This happens both when: * the sub-items are **checkboxes**, or * the sub-items are **bulleted list items** under a parent checkbox item. * (I haven't tested the issue on numbered list items) In edit mode, the parent items briefly appear when clicking into the description field, but after saving again, the parent checkbox remains without any visible text/description. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any work package and edit the description. 2. Insert/create a table in the description. 3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list (task list). 4. Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (i.e., a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. ### What is the buggy behavior? * After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible (their text/description disappears). * The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. * When switching back into edit mode (click into the description), the parent items appear briefly. * After saving again, the parent items disappear again. * In the “code view” of the description, the list elements inside the table appear to be output/rendered incorrectly by OpenProject. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should remain visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables should render consistently in both view mode and edit mode. **Additional notes:** * This seems specifically related to checkbox/task lists **inside tables** combined with **nested** checkbox items. ### Screenshots and other files and ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** * Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** * [ ] Chrome * [x] Firefox * [ ] Safari * [ ] Mobile Safari * [x] Edge **Operating System** * [x] Windows * [ ] Mac OS X * [ ] Mobile iOS * [ ] Mobile Android * [ ] Linux (please specify distro) * [ ] Chrome OS * [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list.

*   Saving again makes parent items disappear.

**OpenProject installation type**
- Packaged installation

16.6.2

- Firefox
- Edge

**Operating System**
- Windows

**Language**
German

*   Open any work package and edit the description.

*   Create a checkbox list in a table cell.
*   Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item.

metadata.originalTicket: ### Description: Several employees reported an issue when using checkbox (task) lists inside a table in a work package description. If a checkbox list item has nested sub-items, the parent (top-level) items become invisible after saving the work package. This happens both when: * the sub-items are **checkboxes**, or * the sub-items are **bulleted list items** under a parent checkbox item. * (I haven't tested the issue on numbered list items) In edit mode, the parent items briefly appear when clicking into the description field, but after saving again, the parent checkbox remains without any visible text/description. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any work package and edit the description. 2. Insert/create a table in the description. 3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list (task list). 4. Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (i.e., a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. ### What is the buggy behavior? * After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible (their text/description disappears). * The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. * When switching back into edit mode (click into the description), the parent items appear briefly. * After saving again, the parent items disappear again. * In the “code view” of the description, the list elements inside the table appear to be output/rendered incorrectly by OpenProject. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should remain visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables should render consistently in both view mode and edit mode. **Additional notes:** * This seems specifically related to checkbox/task lists **inside tables** combined with **nested** checkbox items. ### Screenshots and other files and ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** * Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** * [ ] Chrome * [x] Firefox * [ ] Safari * [ ] Mobile Safari * [x] Edge **Operating System** * [x] Windows * [ ] Mac OS X * [ ] Mobile iOS * [ ] Mobile Android * [ ] Linux (please specify distro) * [ ] Chrome OS * [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

Example table: ### What is the buggy behavior? - Parent checkbox list items become invisible after saving the work package. - The issue occurs when sub-items are checkboxes or bulleted list items. - Parent items briefly appear when clicking into the description field in edit mode. - Saving again removes the parent checkbox text and description. - List elements inside the table render incorrectly in code view. - The bug affects checkbox lists inside tables with nested items. - The reporter has not tested numbered list items. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items and their text remain visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables render consistently in view mode and edit mode. ### Screenshots and other files ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** - Packaged installation **OpenProject version** - 16.6.2 **Browser** - [ ] Chrome - [x] Firefox - [ ] Safari - [ ] Mobile Safari - [x] Edge - [ ] Other (please specify) **Operating System** - [x] Windows - [ ] Mac OS X - [ ] Mobile iOS - [ ] Mobile Android - [ ] Linux (please specify distro) - [ ] Chrome OS - [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** - German

metadata.originalTicket: ### Description: Several employees reported an issue when using checkbox (task) lists inside a table in a work package description. If a checkbox list item has nested sub-items, the parent (top-level) items become invisible after saving the work package. This happens both when: * the sub-items are **checkboxes**, or * the sub-items are **bulleted list items** under a parent checkbox item. * (I haven't tested the issue on numbered list items) In edit mode, the parent items briefly appear when clicking into the description field, but after saving again, the parent checkbox remains without any visible text/description. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any work package and edit the description. 2. Insert/create a table in the description. 3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list (task list). 4. Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (i.e., a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. ### What is the buggy behavior? * After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible (their text/description disappears). * The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. * When switching back into edit mode (click into the description), the parent items appear briefly. * After saving again, the parent items disappear again. * In the “code view” of the description, the list elements inside the table appear to be output/rendered incorrectly by OpenProject. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should remain visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables should render consistently in both view mode and edit mode. **Additional notes:** * This seems specifically related to checkbox/task lists **inside tables** combined with **nested** checkbox items. ### Screenshots and other files and ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** * Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** * [ ] Chrome * [x] Firefox * [ ] Safari * [ ] Mobile Safari * [x] Edge **Operating System** * [x] Windows * [ ] Mac OS X * [ ] Mobile iOS * [ ] Mobile Android * [ ] Linux (please specify distro) * [ ] Chrome OS * [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should stay visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables should render consistently in both view mode and edit mode. **Additional notes:** - This seems specifically related to checkbox/task lists **inside tables** combined with **nested** checkbox items. ### Screenshots and other files and ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** - Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** - [ ] Chrome - [x] Firefox - [ ] Safari - [ ] Mobile Safari - [x] Edge **Operating System** - [x] Windows - [ ] Mac OS X - [ ] Mobile iOS - [ ] Mobile Android - [ ] Linux (please specify distro) - [ ] Chrome OS - [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

It happens when the sub-items are **checkboxes**, and also when the sub-items are **bulleted list items** under a parent checkbox item. I haven't tested numbered list items. In edit mode the parent items briefly show up when you click into the description field. After saving again, the parent checkbox is there but has no visible text/description. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any work package and edit the description. 2. Insert/create a table in the description. 3. Inside a table cell, create a checkbox list (task list). 4. Create nested checkbox sub-items under a parent checkbox item (a parent item with indented sub-items). 5. Save the work package. Here's an example table: ### What is the buggy behavior? - After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible, and their text/description disappears. - The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. - Switching back into edit mode (clicking into the description) makes the parent items appear briefly. - Saving again makes the parent items disappear again. - In the "code view" of the description, the list elements inside the table seem to be output/rendered incorrectly by OpenProject. ### What is the expected behavior? 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) should stay visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables should render consistently in both view mode and edit mode. **Additional notes:** - This seems specifically related to checkbox/task lists **inside tables** combined with **nested** checkbox items. ### Screenshots and other files and ### Environment information **OpenProject installation type** - Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** - [ ] Chrome - [x] Firefox - [ ] Safari - [ ] Mobile Safari - [x] Edge **Operating System** - [x] Windows - [ ] Mac OS X - [ ] Mobile iOS - [ ] Mobile Android - [ ] Linux (please specify distro) - [ ] Chrome OS - [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

Example table: **What is the buggy behavior?** - A few employees ran into this: checkbox (task) lists inside a table in a work package description. - If a checkbox list item has nested sub-items, the parent (top-level) items become invisible after saving the work package. - It happens when the sub-items are checkboxes. - It also happens when the sub-items are bulleted list items under a parent checkbox item. - Numbered list items are not tested. - After saving, the parent checkbox list items are no longer visible and their text disappears. - The checkbox may still be present, but the description is invisible. - In edit mode, the parent items briefly show up when you click into the description field. - Saving again makes the parent items disappear again. - In the "code view" of the description, the list elements inside the table seem to be output incorrectly by OpenProject. - This seems specifically related to checkbox lists inside tables combined with nested checkbox items. **What is the expected behavior?** 1. Parent checkbox list items (and their text) stay visible after saving. 2. Nested checkbox lists inside tables render consistently in view mode and edit mode. **Screenshots and other files** and **Environment information** **OpenProject installation type** - Packaged installation **OpenProject version** 16.6.2 **Browser** - [ ] Chrome - [x] Firefox - [ ] Safari - [ ] Mobile Safari - [x] Edge **Operating System** - [x] Windows - [ ] Mac OS X - [ ] Mobile iOS - [ ] Mobile Android - [ ] Linux (please specify distro) - [ ] Chrome OS - [ ] Other (please specify) **Language** German

### Steps to reproduce

*   Go to the Activity tab on any work package.
*   Access from the Notification center or a work package full view.
*   The bug does not occur when scrolled to the bottom with the Newest at the bottom sort order.

### What is the buggy behavior?

*   This might be a regression.
*   Click once on the comment box in the Activity tab.
*   The box grows in size but keyboard focus does not land in it.

### What is the expected behavior?

*   The click puts keyboard focus on the comment box.

### Screenshots and other files

*   Screenshot from Community.

### Environment information

**OpenProject installation type**

*   Community

**OpenProject version**

*   15.0

**Browser**

*   Firefox

**Operating System**

*   Mac OS X

**Language**

*   EN
